chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam and Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'a, all of them from Aban, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the sale of al-nitaf and al-arba'
He said: And al-arba' is when you make a camel accustomed (to carry water), so it carries water and waters the land, then you become independent of it (by selling it or using it for other purposes).

He said: So do not sell it, but lend it to your neighbor. And al-nitaf is when it has the right to drink (from a specific water source), so you become independent of it; so he says: Do not sell it, but lend it to your brother or your neighbor.

key_terms.النِّطَاف: Water-carrying animals or assets with exclusive drinking rights
key_terms.الْأَرْبَعَاء: A camel accustomed to carrying water for irrigation

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between al-nitaf and al-arba' in the context of selling water animals?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between *al-nitaf* (water rights) and *al-arba'* (a specific water-carrying camel), prohibiting their sale to prevent monopolization while mandating their lending to neighbors for communal benefit. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on *haqq al-sharb* (right of water) as a shared resource rather than a purely commodified asset, prioritizing social equity (*maslaha*) over strict commercial ownership.
